title: Dehydroandrographolide succinate alleviates ulcerative colitis via regulating RAB9A/NF-kappaB axis-mediated macrophage polarization and remodeling the gut microbiota.
authors: Liu, Jiaying; Mai, Yansui; Xie, Yu; Zhou, Xiaoling; Ye, Yiting; Jiang, Dongxu; He, Lian; Ye, Zhandong; Li, Dan; Xia, Chenglai; Su, Jiyan; Huang, Song
journal: Phytomedicine : international journal of phytotherapy and phytopharmacology
one_liner_zh: 该文研究药物DAS通过RAB9A/NF-kappaB轴调节巨噬细胞极化缓解溃疡性结肠炎，虽含分子对接但核心为炎症药理与肠道菌群，非蛋白质-DNA互作或TF-DNA结合建模，与本课题无关。
abstract: BACKGROUND: Dehydroandrographolide succinate (DAS), isolated from Andrographis paniculata, exhibits potent anti-inflammatory activity, yet its therapeutic potential and precise mechanism in ulcerative colitis (UC) remain unexplored. PURPOSE: This study aims to investigate the efficacy and molecular basis that is responsible for the amelioration of DAS against UC. METHODS: Effect of DAS against colitis was studied in a DSS-induced colitis model, and the critical role of macrophage was verified by the macrophage depletion and adoptive macrophage transfer (AMT) model. The anti-inflammation activity of DAS was investigated in the LPS/IFN-gamma-stimulated THP-1-derived macrophage model in vitro, followed by DARTS, CETSA, molecular docking/dynamics, and transcriptomics to elucidate the underlying mechanism. The effect of DAS on gut microbiota was analyzed with metagenomic sequencing. RESULTS: DAS attenuated the colitis features, including weight loss, diarrhea, rectal bleeding, and colon shortening, together with reduced inflammatory infiltrates and restored crypt architecture. DAS down-regulated pro-inflammatory cytokines (IL-1beta, IL-6, TNF-alpha) and up-regulated anti-inflammatory mediators (IL-10, IL-13), meanwhile restoring tight-junction proteins (ZO-1, Occludin) and goblet-cell mucins. Macrophage depletion abolished DAS's benefit, while AMT with DAS-treated macrophages relieved the colitis features, confirming the macrophage-dependency of DAS. Transcriptomics and the following verification revealed that the anti-inflammatory activity of DAS mainly relied on the NF-kappaB signaling pathway by suppressing p65 phosphorylation and downstream targets. DAS inhibited M1 polarization and protected epithelial monolayers from macrophage-mediated damage. Moreover, DAS exhibited high-affinity binding to RAB9A, and RAB9A knockdown abolished DAS-mediated suppression of TLR4/NF-kappaB signaling pathway in macrophages. Metagenomic analysis revealed that DAS treatment enriched Lachnospiraceae bacterium, Duncaniella freteri, Lachnospiraceae bacterium 10-1, Bacterium 1XD8-76, Schaedlerella arabinosiphila, while depleted Muribaculaceae bacterium, Bacteroides intestinalis and Clostridiaceae bacterium. Functional gene profiling indicated that DAS upregulated genes related to butyrate metabolism, amino sugar and nucleotide sugar metabolism, and starch and sucrose metabolism. CONCLUSION: DAS alleviates DSS-colitis by targeting RAB9A to block the NF-kappaB signaling pathway-driven M1 macrophage polarization, and is accompanied by gut microbiota remodeling, highlighting the promising application of DAS against UC.
abstract_zh: 背景：脱氢穿心莲内酯琥珀酸酯（DAS），分离自穿心莲（Andrographis paniculata），具有强效抗炎活性，但其在溃疡性结肠炎（UC）中的治疗潜力及精确机制尚未被探索。目的：本研究旨在探讨DAS改善UC的功效及其分子基础。方法：在DSS诱导的结肠炎模型中研究DAS对结肠炎的作用，并通过巨噬细胞耗竭和过继性巨噬细胞转移（AMT）模型验证巨噬细胞的关键作用。在LPS/IFN-γ刺激的THP-1来源巨噬细胞模型中体外研究DAS的抗炎活性，随后采用DARTS、CETSA、分子对接/动力学及转录组学阐明其潜在机制。通过宏基因组测序分析DAS对肠道菌群的影响。结果：DAS减轻了结肠炎特征，包括体重下降、腹泻、直肠出血和结肠缩短，同时减少炎症浸润并恢复隐窝结构。DAS下调促炎细胞因子（IL-1β、IL-6、TNF-α）并上调抗炎介质（IL-10、IL-13），同时恢复紧密连接蛋白（ZO-1、Occludin）和杯状细胞黏蛋白。巨噬细胞耗竭消除了DAS的益处，而用DAS处理的巨噬细胞进行AMT可缓解结肠炎特征，证实了DAS对巨噬细胞的依赖性。转录组学及后续验证揭示，DAS的抗炎活性主要通过抑制p65磷酸化及其下游靶点，依赖于NF-κB信号通路。DAS抑制M1极化并保护上皮单层免受巨噬细胞介导的损伤。此外，DAS对RAB9A表现出高亲和力结合，且RAB9A敲低消除了DAS介导的巨噬细胞中TLR4/NF-κB信号通路抑制。宏基因组分析显示，DAS处理富集了Lachnospiraceae bacterium、Duncaniella freteri、Lachnospiraceae bacterium 10-1、Bacterium 1XD8-76、Schaedlerella arabinosiphila，同时耗竭了Muribaculaceae bacterium、Bacteroides intestinalis和Clostridiaceae bacterium。功能基因谱分析表明，DAS上调了与丁酸代谢、氨基糖和核苷酸糖代谢以及淀粉和蔗糖代谢相关的基因。结论：DAS通过靶向RAB9A阻断NF-κB信号通路驱动的M1巨噬细胞极化来缓解DSS结肠炎，并伴随肠道菌群重塑，凸显了DAS在UC治疗中的潜在应用前景。
